notes: The mappings point directly to the pinned IEEE 1516.1-2025 API and IEEE 1516.2-2025 standard MIM. Passing installed-package runs are bounded provider evidence, not proof of provider-independent conformance.

requirements.statement: The standard MIM declares HLAtimeManagerState as a required, reliable, receive-order, conditional HLAfederate attribute. Its update condition names Time Advance Request, Time Advance Request Available, Next Message Request, Next Message Request Available, Flush Queue Request, and Time Advance Grant. HLAtimeState is represented by HLAinteger32BE with TimeGranted=0 and TimeAdvancing=1. The portable scenario exercises each of the five request services and observes both standard state values for each successful request/grant cycle; the Flush Queue Request path is verified with its standard Flush Queue Grant callback.
The federate successfully requests a standard logical-time advance and observes the corresponding conditional MOM state transitions.
The federate successfully invokes Time Advance Request Available and observes the standard conditional MOM state transitions through its grant.
The federate successfully invokes Next Message Request and observes the standard conditional MOM state transitions through its grant.
The federate successfully invokes Next Message Request Available and observes the standard conditional MOM state transitions through its grant.
The federate successfully invokes Flush Queue Request and observes the standard conditional MOM state transitions through its grant.
The test verifies that Flush Queue Request completes with exactly one standard Flush Queue Grant rather than a Time Advance Grant, and that both callback logical-time values are present.
The test verifies that each successful advance request produces exactly one Time Advance Grant at the requested logical time while the standard MOM reports TimeGranted.
